material_findings.title: Signed provenance is overstated as protection against a compromised job

candidate_locators.exact_text: Inference: covers the compromised-job claim via signed source, resolved deps, and builder ID.
Minimal check: digest-match subject, verify DSSE signature, enforce trusted `builder.id` set, compare source digest and buildType.

material_findings.finding: Authenticity does not establish tenant-resistant generation. The cited recipe omits generation/control-plane and trusted-level conditions needed to address the brief’s compromised-job threat. Stolen keys and off-map builders do not exhaust this boundary.
material_findings.materiality: A job-controlled claim can remain validly signed by an expected identity without demonstrating the dependency actually used. The assigned mechanism must bound that threat, rather than merely authenticate the statement.
material_findings.supported_scope_to_preserve: Artifact digest, signature, predicate, identity and build-parameter expectations remain useful. No supplier certification, new deployment or universal SLSA level is required by this review.

material_findings.title: Dependency binding omits the best-effort coverage boundary

candidate_locators.exact_text: Inference: covers the compromised-job claim via signed source, resolved deps, and builder ID.

material_findings.finding: The dependency coverage is best effort even through Build L3. A valid statement can omit a consequential dependency; the candidate never records this boundary while crediting dependency binding.
material_findings.materiality: The brief expressly concerns using a different dependency while claiming the correct source. Signed listed dependencies are not a complete account of actual dependencies.
material_findings.supported_scope_to_preserve: Recorded dependencies can be compared against independently selected expectations. The review does not require recursive verification of every dependency or a nonexistent hermetic deployment.

limitations.issue: The named cosign verify-attestation lead is documented for images; local artifact/bundle transport and issuer policy remain unverified. Counted as an implementation lead, not a proven portable installer command; candidate explicitly leaves flags unresolved.
Missing-provenance test assumes a blocked install while block-or-warn remains a product choice. Treat this oracle as conditional, not a decided requirement.

Lockfile/digest mutation does not specify an independent expected dependency or a valid re-attested variant. It could exercise signature, source or subject mismatch instead of dependency policy. This is a prospective ambiguity, not an observed test failure.

in-toto and TUF are real, useful leads with openly acknowledged shallow retrieval. Their field-level applicability was not established by candidate index/overview excerpts; do not credit an executed layout or updater check.

The minimal SLSA recipe does not spell out authorized signer-builder pairing or level-specific trust. A correctly configured trust map could supply this, so no deployed authorization bypass is asserted.
Rekor is principally a signing-event record, not merely a certificate-issuance record. The candidate correctly distinguishes transparency from build correctness; wording alone is not material.

Layout/functionary policy is a distinct alternative; material/product checks connect steps. Formats are separately specified.
TUF contributes channel freshness and authenticated metadata, complementary to build provenance.
